readiness.summary: This app needs changes before Deployz can deploy it.

findings.title: Has no Dockerfile that builds the app
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz builds the image from the repository for every deployment. It cannot build a Dockerfile that is only for development, is a template, or copies files the repository does not contain.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Add a production Dockerfile to the repository that builds and starts the app from source.
findings.technicalEvidence: Unsupported container setup: No Dockerfile exists in the repository. Deployz builds the app from a Dockerfile in the repository.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This repository has no Dockerfile that builds a production image from the source code.

findings.title: Give Deployz a way to check your app
findings.whyItMatters: During every deployment, Deployz waits for your app to report healthy before sending traffic to it. Without a health signal, a broken deploy cannot be detected or rolled back.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Expose a lightweight route (for example /health) that returns success once the app is ready, and reference it from the container health check.
findings.technicalEvidence: No health endpoint or container health check was found (no /health-style route, no HEALTHCHECK instruction).
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: Deployz needs a reliable way to know when your app is running and ready.

findings.title: Your app only listens on localhost
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz sends customer traffic and health checks to the container over the network. A server bound to 127.0.0.1 or localhost never answers them, so every deployment would fail its health check.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Bind the server to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) instead of 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
findings.technicalEvidence: Server binds only to a loopback address: gunicorn bind on a loopback address (contrib/gunicorn.py)
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app accepts connections only from inside its own container, so Deployz cannot reach it.

findings.title: Give Deployz a way to update your database
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs your migration command automatically on every deploy, so each customer database always matches the code that talks to it.
findings.suggestedOutcome: If the app already updates its database when it starts, change nothing. Otherwise set a command that applies the migrations non-interactively in the application settings.
findings.technicalEvidence: A PostgreSQL library is present (psycopg) but no migration command was found in the image start path or any package.json.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app uses a database, but Deployz could not find a command that updates the database structure during deploys.

findings.title: Background job runner
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs each declared worker as its own process. Jobs that need a separate runner do not run until one is declared.
findings.suggestedOutcome: If the web process already runs the jobs, change nothing. Otherwise declare the job runner with its own start command (for example a Procfile worker line).
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app appears to run background jobs, but no command exists that starts a job runner as a separate process.

unsupportedReasons: Unsupported container setup: No Dockerfile exists in the repository. Deployz builds the app from a Dockerfile in the repository.
